title: W.S.W.
subtitle: A Voyage in That Direction to the West Indies
summary: Robert Elwes (1819–1878), a Norfolk landowner and amateur painter who had already published A Sketcher’s Tour round the World, sailed from Southampton with his wife in January 1865 on a Royal Mail steamer and spent three and a half months in the West Indies and at Panama. This is his account of the journey, illustrated with fourteen lithographs from his own drawings.

From St. Thomas they crossed to Colon (Aspinwall) and by the railway to Panama, where they saw the ruins of the old city. They then spent some weeks in Jamaica, staying with Governor Eyre at Flamstead, his house in the Port Royal mountains, a few months before the Morant Bay rising, and went by the islands of St. Kitts, Antigua, Guadeloupe, Dominica, Martinique, St. Vincent, and Grenada to Trinidad, where they stayed sixteen days. He writes about the scenery he sketched, plants, hotels, ships, and fellow passengers. Some of his remarks on the black population, and a footnote in support of Eyre’s suppression of the rising, use the language and views of his time.
